It is sponsored by [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] and known as the '''Emirates FA Cup''' for sponsorship reasons. The FA Cup is the main domestic cup competition for men's football teams in England. The qualifying competition began on 1 August 2025, with the tournament proper starting on 31 October 2025. The [[2026 FA Cup final|final]] was played at [[Wembley Stadium]], [[London]], on 16 May 2026. Defending champions [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], having beaten [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2025 FA Cup final|2025 final]] to win their first ever title, were eliminated in the third round after an [[Macclesfield 2–1 Crystal Palace (2026)|upset victory]] by sixth-tier [[National League North]] side [[Macclesfield F.C.|Macclesfield]].{{Cite web |date=2026-01-10 |title=FA Cup: Macclesfield make history on emotional day |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cy8yqj8jd6yo |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=BBC Sport}} Manchester City, the previous year's finalists, won their 8th FA Cup, defeating [[Premier League]] side [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in what was their fourth consecutive FA Cup Final. ==Teams, dates and regulations== [[File:FA Cup 2025-2026 team progression.svg|thumb|right|Teams in each round.]] The FA Cup is a [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout]] competition with 124 teams taking part from the first round proper, and all trying to reach the final at Wembley Stadium on 16 May 2026. The competition consists of the 92 teams from the Football League system (20 teams from the [[Premier League]] and the 72 in total from the [[EFL Championship]], [[EFL League One]] and [[EFL League Two]]) plus the 32 surviving teams out of 655 teams from the [[National League System]] that started the competition in the [[2025–26 FA Cup qualifying rounds|qualifying rounds]]. The six-round qualifying competition began with the extra preliminary round on 2 August 2025, with the fourth and final qualifying round kicking off on 11 October. The winners from the fourth qualifying round were [[AFC Telford United]], [[AFC Totton]], [[Aldershot Town F.C.|Aldershot Town]], [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]], [[Boreham Wood F.C.|Boreham Wood]], [[Brackley Town F.C.|Brackley Town]], [[Braintree Town F.C.|Braintree Town]], [[Buxton F.C.|Buxton]], [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]], [[Chatham Town F.C.|Chatham Town]], [[Chelmsford City F.C.|Chelmsford City]], [[Chester F.C.|Chester]], [[Eastleigh F.C.|Eastleigh]], [[Ebbsfleet United F.C.|Ebbsfleet United]], [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]], [[Gainsborough Trinity F.C.|Gainsborough Trinity]], [[Gateshead F.C.|Gateshead]], [[FC Halifax Town|Halifax Town]], [[Hemel Hempstead Town F.C.|Hemel Hempstead Town]], [[Macclesfield F.C.|Macclesfield]], [[Maldon & Tiptree F.C.|Maldon & Tiptree]], [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]], [[Slough Town F.C.|Slough Town]], [[South Shields F.C.|South Shields]], [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]], [[Spennymoor Town F.C.|Spennymoor Town]], [[St Albans City F.C.|St Albans City]], [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]], [[Tamworth F.C.|Tamworth]], [[Wealdstone F.C.|Wealdstone]], [[Weston-super-Mare A.F.C.|Weston-super-Mare]] and [[York City F.C.|York City]]. [[Phoenix club (sports)|Phoenix club]] Macclesfield were the only debutants in the first round, appearing in the competition proper for the first time in their own right only five years after the liquidation of predecessor outfit [[Macclesfield Town F.C.|Macclesfield Town]], with Town having last featured in the first round of the FA Cup in [[2017–18 FA Cup|2017–18]].{{cite web |title=FA Cup 2025–26 Q4 Rd Review |url=https://facupfactfile.wordpress.com/2025/10/11/fa-cup-2025-26-q4-rd-review/ |publisher=FA Cup Factfile |access-date=29 October 2025}} Hemel Hempstead Town, South Shields and Spennymoor Town all matched their best ever runs by reaching the competition proper, while Chatham Town featured in the FA Cup for the first time in 97 years. ==First round== A total of 80 teams played in the first round: 32 winners from the fourth qualifying round, 24 from [[EFL League Two|League Two]] (tier 4), and 24 from [[EFL League One|League One]] (tier 3). Eighth tier side [[Maldon & Tiptree F.C.|Maldon & Tiptree]] (Isthmian League North Division) were the lowest-ranked team in the draw.
